column1: # Addresses a fix or a built-in extender feature can override (docs/ENGINE_CRATE.md, "Typed code"): a
# typed function never calls one directly, and typed_call! never names one. Columns: address, the
# direct Rust calls the translations already make to it (a ratchet: repo_hygiene.rs fails on a new one,
# and asks to lower the number when one goes), and what overrides it. Sources: the plugins' literal
# jumps at translated function entries, a lower bound (named constants and run-time addresses are
# missed), nv-rs's own fixes preset (crates/host/src/fixes.rs), and the four fixes-preset guards the audit left.
